rename.from: ind operators like MoreThan and LessThan doesn't work properly for date fields
rename.to: find operators like MoreThan and LessThan doesn't work properly for date fields

body:
Hello guys. I'm still working this issue. I don't know sqlite as well but I did test few cases about comparing datetime values. 

### What's the problem.

```sql
-- 1. getTime() doesn't working, EXPECTED: FALSE, ACTUAL: TRUE
select DATETIME('2019-01-10T00:00:00Z') > 9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999;

-- 2. toUTCString(), doesn't working, EXPECTED: TRUE, ACTUAL: FALSE
select DATETIME('2019-01-10T00:00:00Z') > 'Mon, 31 Dec 2018 15:00:00 GMT';

-- 3. toISOString()
-- Seem to work
-- EXPECTED: TRUE, ACTUAL: TRUE
select DATETIME('2019-01-10T00:00:00Z') > '2019-01-01T00:00:00.000Z';

-- What? Is this about timezone issue?
-- EXPECTED: TRUE, ACTUAL: FALSE
select DATETIME('2019-01-10T08:00:00Z') > '2019-01-10T00:00:00.000Z';

-- SQLite is configured UTC timezone as default on any environment,
-- EXPECTED: 2019-01-01 00:00:00, ACTUAL: 2019-01-01 00:00:00
select DATETIME('2019-01-01T00:00:00Z');

-- DATETIME comparing is working
-- EXPECTED: true, ACTUAL: true
select DATETIME('2019-01-01T00:00:00Z') = DATETIME('2019-01-01T00:00:00Z');
select DATETIME('2019-01-01T01:00:00Z') > DATETIME('2019-01-01T00:00:00Z');

-- 4. Finally I found the root cause.
-- THAT IS JUST STRING COMPARING.
select DATETIME('2019-01-01T12:00:00Z'), -- RESULT: 2019-01-01 12:00:00
       '2019-01-01T00:00:00Z', -- RESULT: 2019-01-01T00:00:00Z
       DATETIME('2019-01-01T12:00:00Z') > '2019-01-01T00:00:00Z', -- false
       DATETIME('2019-01-01T12:00:00Z') > '2019-01-01 00:00:00'   -- true
```

YES, sqlite support ISO 8601 date format, but it's just about insert or update, not about value comparing.
and sqlite doesn't have type to storing date, datetime, timestamp and [that will be stored as `text` type.](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48478112/select-sqlite-date-values-in-iso-8601-format). In my think, `datetype` is just alias for `text`

```sql
-- for date
create table user
(
  id        integer  not null
    primary key autoincrement,
  createdAt datetime not null
);
select typeof(createdAt)
from user;
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9916002/50906711-09337680-1469-11e9-9937-4d097d559de5.png)

### What's the solution.

1. In now, as the best simple solution. format the datetime value.

```typescript
export const MoreThanDate = (date: Date) => MoreThan(format(new Date(), 'yyyy-mm-dd HH:MM:ss.l'))
// ...
const user = await repository.findOne({
    createdAt: MoreThanDate(new Date())
})
```

2. Contribute support datetime in find interface.

@enif-lee 
Hello, I would like to try your MoreThanDate solution but I have a question.

From where come that "format()" function in the MoreThan?

Regards

@bioleyl Uhmm, this is from just simple external node package. 

Try to check below links. :)

1. https://www.npmjs.com/package/dateformat
2. https://www.npmjs.com/package/date-format

Another example, I am using sqlite and the docs say sqlite stores dates like so "TEXT as ISO8601 strings ("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS")."

I needed to find items within a specific date range, I am using moment.js for date manipulations below and I am passing in a normal new Date() object as the startDate and endDate and using moment to covert them to the same string that sqlite stores them as so I can query them easily using typeORM syntax

  ```
const sqliteDateFormat = 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS'
  const startDate = moment(options.startDate).format(sqliteDateFormat)
  const endDate = moment(options.endDate).format(sqliteDateFormat)

  const items = await getConnection()
    .getRepository(ItemsEntity)
    .createQueryBuilder('item')
    .where('item.trackedOn <= :startDate', { startDate })
    .andWhere('item.trackedOn >= :endDate', { endDate })
    .getMany()
```

And this gets many anything within the date ranges I pass in

This is because for persisting, dates are converted particularly:
https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/bc29597eea587d9e4423c86331e7631fe14fd13b/src/driver/sqlite-abstract/AbstractSqliteDriver.ts#L274-L277
but for querying, dates are not specifically handled
https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/bc29597eea587d9e4423c86331e7631fe14fd13b/src/driver/sqlite-abstract/AbstractSqliteDriver.ts#L355-L363
I assume the native sqlite driver then calls `.toISOString()` at some point. SQLite does not have a date type column, datetimes are internally stored as strings. So these two formats are not compatible.

PS: To format a date as a workaround, you can also use typeorm's DateUtil directly instead of crafting your own function:
```ts
import { DateUtils } from 'typeorm/util/DateUtils';
... { MoreThan(DateUtils.mixedDateToUtcDatetimeString(date)
```

issue.body:
### Description of change (copied from commit message)

In sqlite, Date objects are persisted as UtcDatetimeString.
But a Date object parameter was escaped with .toISOString(), making such queries impossible.
This commit aligns both transforms.
This bug does *not* apply to better-sql where you can only bind numbers, strings, bigints, buffers,
and null.
This is breaking for when the user inserted their dates manually as ISO and relied on this old
maltransformation, after this their find()s by Date won't work anymore.

BREAKING CHANGE: Change Date serialization in selects

fixes #2286
